s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative infection of a device implant site with signs of local inflammation and possible systemic infection
salient_findings: Inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site
Elevated inflammatory syndrome on laboratory studies
key_facts: 72-year-old man with no prior medical history
Underwent dual-chamber pacemaker implantation in the left prepectoral area
Procedure was for 2:1 atrioventricular block
Procedure was uneventful
Discharged the next day
Presented with fever (38.1°C) on postoperative day 4
Inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site on postoperative day 4
Laboratory studies revealed an elevated inflammatory syndrome
Blood cultures were obtained
Antibiotics (amoxicillin–clavulanate, 1 g three times daily) were started empirically
Swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis
Lesion darkened and enlarged by day 7 despite antibiotic therapy
Blood cultures remained negative by day 7

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal device infection
shortlist.why_kept: Staphylococcus epidermidis grew from the lesion swab

shortlist.label: Pacemaker pocket infection
shortlist.why_kept: Inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site

shortlist.label: Surgical site infection
shortlist.why_kept: Fever and elevated inflammatory syndrome after surgery

shortlist.label: Prosthetic device infection
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion darkened and enlarged despite antibiotic therapy

shortlist.label: Device-related endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible systemic infection with negative blood cultures

raw.rationale: The patient presented with an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the pacemaker implant site, which is consistent with a pocket infection, and the swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis, a common cause of device-related infections

rejected.label: Staphylococcal device infection
rejected.why: Too broad, as it does not specify the type of device

rejected.label: Surgical site infection
rejected.why: Too general, as it does not account for the specific involvement of the pacemaker device

rejected.label: Prosthetic device infection
rejected.why: Similar to Staphylococcal device infection, it is too broad and does not specify the type of device

rejected.label: Device-related endocarditis
rejected.why: There is no mention of endocardial involvement or valve infection
